target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Current Kew accepts S. eulae as Texas-endemic. County occurrence data derived from TORCH herbarium aggregation includes Bexar, Travis, and San Saba.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; infraspecific records counted only after current-taxonomy reconciliation.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the open panicle and mid-stem leaves. Eula's aster is a rhizomatous Texas endemic with white to pale lavender rays, yellow disks aging reddish-brown, and scabrous elliptic-to-lanceolate leaves with crenate-serrate margins.
